chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad ibn Suheyb who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about some goods in the hands of two men. One of the two is saying, 'I had entrusted it to you', and the other is saying, 'It is a mortgaged item'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The (final) word is the word of those who is saying, 'It is a mortgaged item with me', unless if the one who claims that he had entrusted it were to come with witnesses'.
ai.seo_question: How does Islamic jurisprudence resolve a dispute between two people claiming ownership of the same item under different legal titles?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a pragmatic legal presumption (*istishab*) favoring the possessor's claim of mortgage (*rahn*) over safekeeping (*wadiah*) to protect against false claims of deposit. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that in cases of conflicting claims regarding held property, the status quo is maintained unless the challenger provides definitive proof, thereby prioritizing the security of the asset in the holder's possession. It highlights the practical application of evidentiary standards in commercial disputes within early Islamic society.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abbad Bin Suheyb who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about some goods in the hands of two men. One of the two is saying, ‘I had entrusted it to you’, and the other is saying, ‘It is a mortgaged item’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The (final) word is the word of those who is saying, ‘It is a mortgaged item with me’, unless if the one who claims that he had entrusted it were to come with witnesses’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abbad ibn Suhayb who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of two men who disputed about an asset. One said that it was a Wadi ‘ah (safe deposit) and the other said that it was al-Rahn (security deposit). Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The words of one who says that it is al-Rahn (security deposit) are accepted unless the other party presents witnesses who testify that it is Wadi ‘ah (safe deposit).”’
